bottom_line: The ratings were made before this week's export licensing and Monday's 5% semis drop, and Nvidia reports after tonight's close, so the open is the worst-informed moment to act. Futures are only mildly mixed, but the worldview's top risk lands within hours: wait for Nvidia's print and guide before adding.
what_changed: US futures mixed to slightly lower before the open: Dow E-minis about -0.45% and S&P -0.34% at 5:23 ET, with Nasdaq-100 futures later up about 0.5% after Monday's -2.5% (Reuters, Yahoo Finance).

Nvidia reports fiscal Q3 after tonight's close, its first print since Huang resigned, against guidance of ~$108bn revenue that already assumes no China data-centre sales (FXStreet, TradingKey). This is the worldview's top named risk.
New US licences for AI chip sales to Southeast Asia and Brazil hit the export-risk thesis (stronger, 84) and weigh most on AMAT, ASML and ANET.
Monday's selloff reached power and cooling too (-4.4% and -3.8%), so the bottleneck names were not a refuge this week.

trust: None of the 54 picks are graded yet (grading starts after 28 days). So far picks rated Buy/Overweight average -2.1% vs QQQ, ahead of the no-AI screen (-7.5%) and random shortlist (-4.3%) but behind simply holding QQQ.
if_buying: Overweight means a small starting position only; nothing tonight justifies more.
If acting at all, favour grid (PWR, ETN), which held best, and use limit orders near the last close.
Wait on AMAT, ASML, ANET, VRT and DELL until Nvidia's guide and export commentary are out after the close.
Expect a volatile open with VIX at 22.6; avoid market orders in the first 30 minutes.
